title: LucentGrid POC acceptance criteria + security alignment
summary: Kickoff to align on POC acceptance criteria, sizing for expected workloads (inference qps / concurrency), security gating (SOC 2 + ISO checklist), SSO/SAML integration and required RBAC, and audit log retention/KMS expectations. Agreed next steps include sending a concise security playbook, a baseline benchmark plan, and scheduling a short on-prem/VPC install walkthrough.
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel - Send SOC 2 + ISO executive summary and Redwood private deployment checklist - Due: 2027-02-16
Owner: Ethan Cole - Draft benchmark plan (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cold vs warm cache) and sample test harness scripts - Due: 2027-02-18
Owner: Priya Menon - Provide representative workload (sample prompts + expected concurrency patterns, token lengths) and synthetic dataset - Due: 2027-02-15
Owner: Omar Reyes - Share compliance requirements doc (retention windows, encryption standards, KMS/HSM policies) and SSO IdP metadata - Due: 2027-02-14
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + short private deployment notes
Customer to deliver workload samples and IdP metadata
Schedule 60-min benchkick (shared spreadsheet) for the week of 2027-02-22
Confirm procurement timeline and PO trigger (Tom)
transcript:
Meeting: 2027-02-11 16:00 UTC - Duration 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rina (CSM) -- Nina (VP Eng), Omar (SecOps), Priya (ML Eng), Tom (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros and then we'll jump to acceptance criteria. Uh, Nina are you leading on the success criteria side?
[00:12] Nina: Yeah thanks, hi all, hi Maya, Ethan. So for LucentGrid we need to validate three things in the pilot: first functional parity for routing and prompt handling, second performance under our 250 concurrent sessions peak, and third security and auditability - SOC 2 style controls and SSO integration.
[00:30] Ethan: Great, can I ask a quick clarifying q, when you say 250 concurrent, is that hard concurrency or sessions with long polling? Like are these streaming sessions?
[00:40] Priya: Mostly short-turn chat like 60-120 token responses, some longer 600-800 token generation for summarization, and yes streaming is important for UX. Concurrency is around 250 active connections, QPS about 120 sustained, bursts to 300 for a minute or two.
[01:01] Maya: good, that's helpful. We'll propose a baseline benchmark that includes p50/p95 latency, and throughput targets. Our typical private deployment config for that footprint is-- sorry Rina interjects--
[01:12] Rina: and just to note we have autoscale + burst on Dedicated but for Private VPC it depends on infra.
[01:18] Omar: security front, a few must-haves: SOC 2 type II equivalence, ISO 27001 evidence preferred, SSO with SAML2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC scoped to environment and model, and full audit logs with immutable retention for at least 1 year. Also KMS integration for envelope encryption.
[01:36] Ethan: Understood. For SOC 2 / ISO we can provide our audit artifacts and an executive summary. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments and can outline key rotation flow.
[01:48] Omar: How granular are your audit logs? We need token-level attribution back to the user identity and model version, plus tamper-evidence.
[01:55] Ethan: We capture request id, caller identity (via token claims or SSO subject), model id/version, full request/metadata and, depending on config, truncated payloads. We can retain logs on the customer's S3/GCS bucket with lifecycle policies. There may be redaction options for PII in transit though that's part of the workload design.
[02:14] Nina: retention - we can't keep raw content beyond 90 days in some markets, but audit metadata must stay 1 year. Is redaction configurable so we can keep logs for auditing but redact text?
[02:25] Maya: Yes, we typically separate audit metadata from payload. We can discuss a configuration where full payloads are off by default, metadata retained longer; also we can support routed copies to customer-owned bucket for retention policies.
[02:38] Tom: procurement question, timeline - we need an internal security review first before a PO. What's a realistic pilot start date if we move quickly?
[02:45] Maya: If all artifacts are shared promptly, we can start benchkick in ~2 weeks and have a 4-week pilot. So start date target week of 2027-02-22 and wrap by mid-March.
[02:56] Priya: on benchmarks can you lay out cold vs warm cache numbers? Our models are GPT-style decoder models, KV cache matters for warm starts.
[03:07] Ethan: Absolutely. Bench plan will include cold start latency (first token), warm cached latency (p50/p95), and throughput tests with continuous batching. We'll also test prefix caching for repeated prompts. We'll attach scripts - note sometimes transcribe as redwood runtime does continuous batching which lowers per-token cost.
[03:26] Nina: about environment isolation - we want a VPC-deployed private control plane. Is there a lightweight control plane that still gives us RBAC and tracing hooks?
[03:35] Ethan: The Private offering runs a control plane that can be customer-hosted in your VPC. It exposes RBAC, per-model routes, and tracing hooks (trace id injected). We can provide SSO mapping to Azure AD or Okta and SCIM provisioning.
[03:49] Omar: any third-party pen test or do you provide SOC 2 report only? We might require a pen test summary for the specific setup.
[03:57] Maya: We have a SOC 2 Type II report and can share redacted pen test summaries. For on-prem/private deployments we offer assistance during our onboarding pen test window and can coordinate a scoped test with your team.
[04:12] Priya: data residency — we have EU customers; for this pilot data must stay in eu-west-1. Can Private run in their region?
[04:20] Ethan: Yes we can deploy in customer VPC in eu-west-1 region or on-prem; we'll note network egress requirements in the checklist.
[04:27] Tom: SLAs - during pilot we don't need a formal SLA but need reliability targets for acceptance.
[04:33] Maya: Acceptance criteria doc will include uptime thresholds (>=99% over bench window), p95 latency <= 500ms for short responses, and throughput targets per your sample workload. We'll put those into the success criteria spreadsheet.
[04:46] Nina: Can you also capture cost estimate per 1M tokens and per-hour reserved capacity so we can budget?
[04:53] Maya: Yes, we'll provide rough unit economics for both hosted and private (GPU-backed) configurations and show sensitivity to batching and quantization.
[05:02] Omar: SSO integration detail - we need SAML metadata and SCIM for group sync into RBAC. Also, audit trail must show which group made changes to model versions.
[05:12] Ethan: We'll map SAML attributes to RBAC and log admin actions with subject and group info. Model rollouts are logged as events with before/after model ids.
[05:21] Priya: any gotchas with HSM/KMS in private - rotation frequency and access patterns?
[05:28] Ethan: Customer KMS supports envelope keys, we don't hold plaintext root keys. Rotation is handled per your KMS policy; we document the handshake and access control. If you require HSM-backed keys in your HSM we can integrate via standard KMS providers.
[05:42] Rina: quick note, we'll share a short 1-pager that maps compliance asks to artifacts we can provide.
[05:48] Maya: Okay to recap - Redwood sends security pack (SOC2/ISO exec summary + private deployment notes), Ethan sends bench plan and test scripts, LucentGrid sends workload samples and IdP metadata, Omar sends retention/KMS specifics. We aim to kick bench the week of 2/22.
[06:04] Tom: sounds good, I'll start procurement gating and let you know PO timeline.
[06:09] Nina: thanks, one last question, competitors - we're also testing a Bedrock path and an internal inference stack. How do you help compare cost/perf?
[06:18] Maya: We'll include a short comparison matrix and run the same benchmark harness so apples-to-apples. We'll also highlight where our routing and caching gives unit cost benefits.
[06:28] Maya: Alright we'll follow up with the pack and schedule the benchkick. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] End meeting
questions: What are the pilot success criteria and timeline?
Can Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning?
How granular are audit logs and retention options?
Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments?
